Higher Priced Mortgage Loans (HPML)
OVERVIEW
Higher Priced Mortgage Loans (HPML) are defined as consumer-purpose, closed-end loans secured by a
consumer s principal dwelling that have an annual percentage rate (APR) equal to or greater than the Average
Prime Offer Rate (APOR) by 1.5 percentage points for first-lien loans, or 3.5 percentage points for subordinate-
lien loans for a comparable transaction. For example:
  If the APR on a first lien transaction is equal to or greater than APOR + 1.5%, the loan will be
considered a Higher Priced Mortgage Loan.
  If the APR on a subordinate lien transaction is equal to or greater than APOR + 3.5%, the loan will be
considered a Higher Priced Mortgage Loan.
The Average Prime Offer Rate (APOR) is published by the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
once per week. The APOR for the week the interest rate is locked is the APOR that must be used to
determine if a loan is a Higher Priced Mortgage Loan (HPML).
Certain products are eligible to be closed as a Higher Priced Mortgage Loan (HPML).
  If the APR on a loan falls into the HPML category, the product must be eligible in order to close and
fund.
  If the product is ineligible, the APR must be reduced in order to close and fund.
EFFECTIVE DATE
The rule was effective for all mortgage applications taken on or after October 1, 2009.
ELIGIBLE PRODUCTS
Certain products may be closed as a higher priced mortgage loan. Eligible products, including the 5427
Advantage will not have any system restrictions at the time of locking the interest rate, clear to close status in
Underwriting, etc. Please refer to the ineligible product section to determine if a product is eligible or ineligible.
Please note, loans that are considered Higher Priced Mortgage Loans (HPML) will not be eligible for an
Escrow Waiver.
INELIGIBLE PRODUCTS
Loans with the following characteristics are not eligible to close as a Higher Priced Mortgage Loan (HPML).
These loans may close below the maximum allowable APR so that the loan is not considered HPML.
Additional products may be ineligible due to the ATR/QM rule. Please refer to the Qualified Mortgage section
within Compliance, Doc. #4801 for specific products.

--- Page 2 ---
Higher Priced Mortgage Loans (HPML)
SYSTEM BLOCKS FOR INELIGIBLE PRODUCTS
The Loantrac system will restrict a user in the following situations:
  Rate Lock   On ineligible products if APR exceeds the max HPML APR then the loan will not lock and
will be returned to the previous status before the attempted lock (i.e. floating, expired, lock extension,
etc.)
  Final Approval Clear to Close Status   On ineligible products, if the max HPML APR exceeds, then the
Underwriter will be unable to place the loan in a Final Approval Clear to Close status until the HPML
APR is at or below the maximum HPML APR.
  Closing Documents (WBCD)   User will be able to draw closing documents from WBCD, however an
error message will be displayed referencing a Section 35 error. The user will be unable to continue until
the HPML APR is at or below the maximum HPML APR.
  Funding   User will be unable to request funding until the HPML APR is at or below the maximum
HPML APR.
When locking loans all fees should be accurate to ensure a valid lock. If fees change after locking the loan and
a HPML error is present, the error can only be fixed by:
  Reducing the interest rate (may result in a worst-case pricing scenario)
  Reducing or removing originator fees, if applicable (i.e. origination, points)
  Apply lender credits
Ineligible products will display the maximum allowable APR on the following screens in Loantrac:
  Registration Confirmation
  Disclosure Compliance
  Underwriting Condition (prior to or at close)
CORRESPONDENT LOCK-IN DATE
A field is available upon initial lock and in the Lock Extension module that will allow correspondents to input a
"true" lock in date in instances where a correspondent confirms a lock-in with the borrower on a different day
than it is locked in Loantrac. This will ensure the correct APOR is used when identifying if the loan is a Higher
Priced Mortgage Loan.
IV. Policies and Procedures 2 of 2 Document #4813
10/17/2022

One-Close Construction Eligibility Standards
PROGRAM SUMMARY
Flagstar s Conforming One-Close Construction, Doc #5717 is a conforming one-time close 6, 9 or 12 month
construction term program allowing for payment of interest-only during construction. The Jumbo One Close
Construction, Doc. #5724 is a 12, 18, and 24 month term program. The note will be modified upon completion
of improvements to a fully amortized principal and interest payment. Soft costs (architectural, engineering and
permit fees) may be financed, closing costs may not. Full third party builder contracts only. All loans close in
the name of Flagstar Bank.
SPONSORSHIP
Customers must be sponsored by their Flagstar Account Executive to participate in Flagstar s construction
programs.
TRAINING
All loan originators and processors involved in the origination of Flagstar s products must attend a mandatory
training session prior to receiving eligibility to register and submit loans. Training sessions are hosted by
Flagstar s Lending Training team on a regular basis via webinar.
VOLUME
Flagstar will require origination of a minimum of 4 construction loans in 12 month period following training for
customers to remain eligible to originate the product. Volume will be measured at a company level.
ORIGINATOR RESPONSIBILITIES
Originators will be required to attend a call with Flagstar s Construction department approximately one week
prior to close to set expectations with all parties, including the borrower and the builder.
Additionally, from time to time Flagstar may ask for the customer s assistance to contact the borrower for
additional information during or after the construction period, i.e. after closing.
REQUALIFICATION
Under the parameters of the program, borrowers may be required to requalify for the loan as construction is
being completed. All jumbo loans will be requalified. See product description for complete details.
In the event a borrower needs to requalify, a Flagstar sales assistant will be contacting the originator once
construction is approximately 75% complete. The originator will have the option of contacting borrower directly
or having Flagstar sales assistant coordinate to obtain necessary documentation from the borrower (e.g.
income, assets, etc.) for requalification.
ELIGIBILITY
Notwithstanding the training and minimum volume requirements, Flagstar in its sole discretion reserves the
right to terminate eligibility for originators and/or customers to originate its One-Close Construction product.
REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES
All representation and warranties included in Flagstar s Loan Purchase Agreement and Sellers Guide remain in
full force and effect.

CONTINUITY OF OBLIGATION
For a refinance transaction (either rate and term/limited cash-out or cash-out), there must be a continuity of
obligation if there is currently an outstanding lien that will be satisfied through the refinance transaction.
An acceptable Continuity of Obligation exists when any of the following exist:
  There is at least one (1) Borrower obligated on the new loan who was also a Borrower obligated on
the existing loan that is being refinanced;
  The Borrower has been on title and residing in the property for at least six (6) months and has
either paid the mortgage for the last six (6) months or can demonstrate a relationship (parent,
spouse, domestic partner, sibling, etc.) with the current obligor;
  The Borrower has recently inherited or was legally awarded the property (divorce, separation); or
  The existing loan being refinanced and the title have been held in the name of a natural person or a
limited liability company as long as the Borrower was a member of the limited liability company prior
to transfer. The loan must have been transferred out of Limited Liability Company prior to
application. Transfer of ownership from a corporation to individual does not meet Continuity of
Obligation.

Escrow Waiver Eligibility Guidelines
ELIGIBILITY
Flagstar Bank will consider a request for a tax and homeowner insurance escrow waiver. Underwriting will
evaluate the request during the credit review and issue the escrow waiver approval prior to closing.
REQUIREMENTS
All escrow waiver requests must meet the following requirements:
  LTV must be 80% or less 1
  Allowable on owner occupied and second home properties with an Accept or Approve from LPA/DU
and a minimum credit score of 620. No assets other than those required by LP/DU need to be verified.
  Allowable on investment properties with an Accept or Approve from LP/DU and a minimum credit score
of 700. LPA/DU required assets, in addition to one-year of taxes, must be verified.
Escrow waivers are subject to underwriting approval and are not allowed on loans requiring Mortgage
Insurance. 1
1. Due to state law, for California loans only, escrow waivers are permitted up to a 90% LTV; however, mortgage insurance must be escrowed by Flagstar
Bank. Under no circumstances, in any state, can mortgage insurance escrows be waived when MI is required.
RESTRICTIONS
  Flood insurance must be included in the borrowers escrow account even if all other escrows have been
waived.
  If the borrower is not establishing an escrow account, an upcoming tax payment or insurance payment
is not allowed to be rolled into the new loan amount on a rate and term transaction unless requiring an
escrow account is prohibited by a state law or regulation. For cash out transactions, the loan amount
cannot include the financing of real estate taxes when the taxes are more than 60 days delinquent if
escrows are being waived.
  It is the responsibility of the originator to understand and be in compliance with individual state
regulations regarding escrow waivers and fees.
  Transactions considered HPML per Compliance procedures, Doc. #4801, are not eligible for an escrow
waiver.
The standard escrow provision must remain in the mortgage documents. Flagstar Bank may, at its discretion,
enforce the requirement if the borrower fails to act responsibly.
SUBMISSION
If the borrower(s) are requesting an escrow waiver, the request can be applied or revoked by the lender within

There is a loan level price adjustment for an escrow waiver on correspondent loans (there is no adjustment on
broker loans) in lieu of an escrow waiver fee. The price adjustment can be found on our Price Indication
Sheets and/or Flagstar Pricing Engine. There are no adjustments for partial escrow waivers if only homeowner
insurance is waived.
DISCLOSURES
If the escrow waiver is approved, it is the obligation of the borrower to pay the amounts for any and all escrow
items when due, in addition to paying the mortgage loan payment.
The lender shall have the right to establish or re-establish an escrow account for the payment of the escrow
items in accordance with the terms of the loan documents in the event that during the term of the mortgage
loan:
  The borrower fails to pay any of the escrow items in a prompt and timely manner.
  The borrower fails to provide the lender with evidence of payment of the escrow items within two weeks
following the receipt of a written request from the lender.
  The borrower is otherwise in default under the terms of the mortgage loan documents.
  It becomes necessary for the lender to advance funds to pay all or any portion of the escrow Iiens.
If the borrower fails to maintain any of the required insurance coverage, the lender may opt to obtain insurance
coverage at the borrower s expense. Such coverage shall cover the lender, but might or might not protect the
borrower. The cost of the insurance coverage obtained by the lender might exceed the cost of insurance the
borrower could have obtained. Any amounts paid by the lender shall be the responsibility of the borrower.

Hybrid eClose allows the borrower(s) to view and electronically sign the majority of their closing package
ahead of the scheduled closing. The Closing Agent or Notary will only bring the documents requiring an ink
signature (Note, Mortgage and any other documents requiring a Notary signature) to the scheduled closing.

closing prior to the scheduled closing appointment.

o

Hybrid eClose Quick Reference Guide
ABC Broker
OUTLINE OF THE FLAGSTAR HYBRID e CLOSE PROCESS
1. TPO Customer - preparing for eClosing
a. Confirm Settlement Agent (SA) is prepared to conduct an eClosing.
b. Obtain approval from eligible borrowers willing to participate in a Hybrid eClosing.
c. When scheduling the closing remind the SA and the borrower the loan will eClose.
d. Generate the Initial CD, as per the current process, confirm the Borrower eClose Approval
reflects Yes (if borrower wishes to eClose) on the Closing/Document Request page in Loantrac.
Follow the same steps for requesting audit review.
e. Collaboration with the SA.
i. Remind the SA the loan will be eSigned.
ii. When providing the SA with the Closing Disclosure, Mortgage, Note, riders, payoff, HOI
also include the Tips for a Smooth eClose Process document.
f. Releasing the final eClose package
i. Once the collaboration with the SA is complete and all closing conditions have been
submitted, select  Request Document Review  to notify the ABC team the package is
ready for review and releasing documents.
ii. The Auditor will review the closing package and, upon approval, select the Hybrid
eClose package option which will notify both the SA and borrower that documents
are available to be signed.
iii. When the final closing package is released, the Closing Package History is
available on the Pickup Closing Docs page providing visibility into the type of closing
package sent (Paper or Hybrid) as well as the participant signing status for Hybrid
closings.
iv. If opted in to receive the eClose Package released to Borrower email alert, you
will also receive notification when Closing Services releases the Hybrid eClose
package.
2. Executing the closing
a. Borrower will review and electronically sign the notices and disclosures prior to the scheduled
closing time. NOTE: The eSign experience for the borrower is the same eSign experience as the
application disclosures.
b. SA will ensure Notary has copies of the documents requiring wet signature only prior to the loan
closing.
c. SA will confirm all borrowers have completed eSigning the package on the day of closing.
d. SA will electronically sign the documents requiring SA signature.
e. SA or Notary will meet with the borrower to complete the signing of documents requiring ink
signatures.
3. After closing
a. Notary returns wet signed documents to the SA.
b. eSigned closing package is automatically retrieved and will be available in Documents under the
ESIGNED MULTIPLE DOCUMENTS Document Type once all participants have completed the
eSigning of the documents.
c. SA returns wet signed documents back to Flagstar per the SA instructions (only the wet-
signed documents).
Please email BrokerABC@flagstar.com with any question related to the Hybrid eClose.

Title Insurance Policy Requirements
TITLE INSURANCE
Title insurance protects the lender and borrower against financial loss from defects in title to real property and
from the invalidity or unenforceability of mortgage loans. Title insurance will defend against a lawsuit attacking
the title or reimburse the insured for the actual monetary loss incurred up to the dollar amount of insurance
provided by the policy.
The Title Policy must be issued on the most recent American Land Title Association (ALTA) policy form, and
must not contain creditor s rights exclusion language adopted by ALTA. Short Form Title should be used on all
eligible loans and should be included in the closing package.
In general, the basic elements of insurance protect the lender from losses from the following matters:
  The title to the property on which the mortgage is being made is either:
Not in the mortgage loan borrower,
o
Subject to defects, liens or encumbrances, or
o
Unmarketable.
o
  There is no right of access to the land
  The lien created by the mortgage:
is invalid or unenforceable,
o
is not prior to any other lien existing on the property on the date the policy is written, or
o
is subject to mechanic's liens under certain circumstances
o
There are (2) types of policies available:
  A Lenders policy that protects the lender in case of title or ownership issues and ensures the
marketability of the property
  An Owner s policy which the borrower may obtain to protect their equity in the property in case of title or
ownership issues
Flagstar requires a Lenders policy for at least the current principal balance of the mortgage for all non HELOC
residential transactions (excludes Cooperatives)
HELOC TITLE INSURANCE
Home Equity Lines of Credit (HELOC) with loan amounts < $500,000.00 require a property report from Title
365 or Flagstar approved HELOC title provider for standalone products (not closing in conjunction with a first
mortgage). Please refer to the HELOC product guidelines for loan amounts > $500,000.00

Exceptions for subsurface public utility easements for local residential distribution, such as lines for gas
and water, and cable for electric, telephone, or CATV utilities, are acceptable provided that the location

with the use and enjoyment of any present improvements on the mortgaged premises or proposed

that is not attached to, or a portion of, the dwelling structure are acceptable provided that the
encroachments do not interfere with the use and enjoyment of the easements or the exercise of rights of
repair and maintenance in connection therewith, and the borrowers have executed a Hold Harmless Letter.

Guidelines for Down Payment Assistance Programs
DOWN PAYMENT ASSISTANCE PROGRAM GENERAL INFORMATION
Down payment assistance (DPA) can take a variety of forms: gift funds, grant money, secured loans
(hereinafter referred to as Community Seconds) and unsecured loans. Down payment assistance programs
are used to provide funds for down payment, closing costs and/or prepaids. The information below will:
  Define the difference between a Community Second program and a Gift/Grant program,
  Describe how to register loans with a Community Second or Gift/Grant in Flagstar s Loantrac System,
  Describe how the underwriter needs to address the different types of programs when running through
the automated underwriting system(s), and
  Describe how the underwriter is to condition for the particular programs at loan closing.
Many in the industry refer to all down payment assistance programs as grants when in fact the vast majority of
DPA programs are structured as secured loans. Unsecured loans are not addressed within these guidelines
and should be reviewed by the underwriter according to the applicable investor criteria.
Flagstar publishes separate lists of eligible Community Second programs and Gift/Grant programs. Refer to
Community Seconds Programs, Doc. #5932 and Gift/Grant Programs, Doc. #5935.
How to determine if a program is a Community Second or a Gift/Grant:
  Is a lien filed in the property records?
  Do the guidelines mention that the transaction is a  loan  or that a  retention agreement  is filed?
If any type of lien is filed the DPA program is considered a Community Second loan and not a Gift/Grant. The
loan amount must be considered in the CLTV, and if any payments are required in the first five years (three
years for FHA) the payment must be included in the borrower s debt-to-income (DTI) ratio.
ELIGIBLE PROGRAM PROVIDERS
  Government entities (states, counties, cities, etc.), government agencies, or instrumentalities of
government
  Verifiable non-profit agencies (a 501(c)3 letter is required for verification)
  Employers (through an established employer-assisted housing program)
INELIGIBLE PROGRAM PROVIDERS
  Seller funded
  Broker funded
  Realtor funded
  Builder funded
  For profit entities
The listing of a program on either of the above lists does not override the requirements of the product
description or underwriting guidelines.
Cash back to the borrower is prohibited on a Community Seconds transaction.
V. Product Guidelines 1 of 7 Document #5936

--- Page 2 ---
Guidelines for Down Payment Assistance Programs
COMMUNITY SECONDS PROGRAMS
Community Seconds programs are loans secured by the subject property. The loan may or may not be
forgiven at the end of the loan term. A Note (sometimes referred to as a Loan Agreement or other name) is
signed at closing, and a Deed of Trust/Mortgage or a Deed Restriction is filed to secure the loan. Repayment
terms must always be reviewed by Flagstar for compliance with Fannie Mae, Freddie Mac and HUD
guidelines. The agency providing the assistance must provide an award/approval letter to the underwriter,
outlining the exact amount of the assistance and the repayment terms. While the loan may be forgiven after a
specified retention period, some programs require the loan to be paid off upon sale of the property, and in
some instances payments are required during the term of the loan. If a payment is required within the first five
years (three years for FHA) the payment must be considered in the borrower s DTI.
Flagstar will allow more than one Community Second loan to be used with a Flagstar first mortgage as long as
the CLTV does not exceed the maximum allowed by the first mortgage loan program.
BELOW MARKET RATE PROGRAMS (BMR)
Below market rate programs are reviewed in the same manner as a Community Second. BMR programs
generally have a non-monetary Note, Mortgage and Restrictive Covenant associated.
GIFT/GRANT PROGRAMS
Gift or Grant programs require no repayment and no lien is filed in the property records. These types of funds
are provided by a government agency, a verified nonprofit agency or the borrower s employer. If the
award/approval letter states a lien will be taken on the property (even if all payments are deferred) the program
is considered a Community Second. Gift/Grant assistance is entered as an asset on the 1003 in Loantrac.
Another type of grant program is an Individual Development Account (IDA). In most cases these programs do
not have any recapture provision. When they do have a recapture provision, they are considered Community
Seconds.
COMMUNITY SECONDS REQUIRING LENDER PARTICIPATION
Many organizations offering down payment assistance require lenders to become approved with them in order
to participate in the DPA program. Lender participation can include, but is not limited to:
  An agreement must be signed (agreements have requirements that must be able to be met)
  Training for the program must take place
  The program underwriting guidelines must be followed (even if different than the first mortgage program
guidelines).
  A financial contribution may be required (whether it is an annual fee or a commitment fee)
Flagstar guidelines state,  Any lender participation required by the program would require the
broker s/correspondent s approval for participation.  In essence this means, the broker or correspondent is
responsible for the relationship and whatever it entails with the DPA provider. Flagstar will not itself become
approved with any DPA provider.
Flagstar reviews programs to determine if we can comply with the first mortgage investor guidelines for
compliance purposes only.

REGISTRATION AND UNDERWRITING GUIDELINES
Eligible programs are entered in Loantrac as Affordable/Community Seconds.
The Affordable Community Seconds Repayment Type is then chosen based on whether the payments are
forgiven or not.
Payments must be deferred for a minimum of five years (conventional) or three years (FHA) or the payment
must be included in the DTI. The approval letter from the DPA provider must be provided to the Underwriter
outlining the exact dollar amount and the repayment terms of the Community Second. Underwriting must
include an  at close  condition for the secondary lien. If more than one Community Second is to be used on an
individual loan, each subordinate lien must be conditioned separately with the name of the lien holder and the
dollar amount of the Community Second lien. (Conditions should be the same for a Community Second lien as
it would be for any subordinate financing).

Loan Registration and Locking a Loan - Correspondent
HOW TO OBTAIN RATE & PRICE QUOTES
Flagstar Bank reserves the right to change rates, prices and fees quoted for any mortgage product at any time
during the day. The actual rates, prices and fees applicable to a given commitment will be those in effect at the
time the commitment is obtained.
Flagstar publishes daily price indications at 10 a.m. Eastern Time, should market conditions warrant a change
new price indication sheets will be published and posted at tpo.flagstar.com. It is our intention to notify
customers by e-mail when rates move; however, rates are subject to change at any time without notice.
The most current Price Indications are always available at tpo.flagstar.com.
Please make sure that you click  refresh  or  reload  to make sure that your browser is displaying the most
current price indication sheets.
EMAIL
Please be aware that you will only receive Price Indications via email at 10 a.m. Eastern Time.
WEBSITE
Once you are logged into our website, click on Price a Loan under the Rates & Pricing menu. Price a Loan
allows you to enter loan specific details to obtain a price indication on one product or compare pricing on
multiple products. From Price a Loan, you can also register and lock a loan.
HOW TO REGISTER/LOCK A LOAN
WEBSITE
Log on to our website and select the Register New Loan to import your registration file or input loan
registration information. If you do not see this option, contact your website Administrator (usually an officer
of your company) to have your user profile updated with this feature.
CALYX POINT
You can use this loan origination system to lock and import your loans directly to Flagstar. Please contact
your Account Executive for more details.
FAX
You may lock a loan by faxing Flagstar Bank s Lock Desk any business day from 10:00 a.m. to Midnight
Eastern Time. To register and/or lock by fax, you must complete the Loan Registration and Lock Request,
Doc. #3101 in its entirety and fax to (248) 312-LOCK (5625).
PHONE
To lock by phone call: (866) 945-9872
Follow customer service prompts to speak with a Rate Lock Specialist.
REQUIRED REGISTRATION/LOCK INFORMATION
When registering or locking a loan, you must provide the following:
1. Company name, seller ID number, and phone number.
2. Contact person
3. Borrower s name
4. Borrower s Social Security Number
IV. Policies and Procedures 1 of 6 Document #4121
08/03/2022

5. Co-borrower s name
6. Co-borrower s Social Security Number
7. Loan purpose
8. Property address
9. City, county, state, zip code
10. Loan amount
11. Purchase price and/or estimated value
12. Property type
13. Occupancy
14. Lock period
15. Loan product
16. Interest rate
17. Rate sheet pricing
If all information is accurate, a loan number will be assigned. When confirmation is received (available
online), please check for accuracy and report any discrepancies to our Lock Desk immediately. It is the
exclusive obligation of the contact to review and communicate any errors to Flagstar Bank upon receipt.
Loans may be registered at any time after the preliminary application is taken. The correspondent may
choose to float the loan or lock according to lock periods specified for each product on the price indication
sheet.
Please note the following:
  All loan products have price caps
  Some loan products must be approved before they can be locked
Refer to price indication sheets for additional details.
LOCK-IN TERMS
Flagstar Bank offers lock in commitment terms between 15 and 90 days without any additional upfront fee, as
well as extended lock in commitments ranging between 120 and 365 days depending on the product type. All
lock in commitments greater than 90 days will require an upfront fee. Please review Correspondent Lock
Extension Policy, Doc. #4122 for details. Certain products offer the delivery choice of best efforts or
mandatory. The mandatory lock-in commitment requires that the loan be closed, disbursed and note and post-
closing package received by Flagstar exactly as locked according to Flagstar s on time delivery outlined in
Correspondent Lock Extension Policy, Doc. #4122. Failure to deliver a mandatory commitment will result in a
pair-off of that commitment. The best efforts lock-in commitment will be considered mandatory if a loan locked-
in with Flagstar closes with Correspondent but is not delivered. If the borrower withdraws his or her application
and does not close with Correspondent, Correspondent shall provide a copy of Notice of Credit Denial to
Flagstar Bank upon request.
TO BE DETERMINED (TBD) PROPERTY ADDRESS
A lock may be committed on a TBD property address for a period of 60-90 days on eligible products. Only
eligible products and lock periods will be displayed when the TBD property address question has been
selected as Yes on the main registration page. A property address must be provided and updated within the
loan registration at least 30 days prior to initial lock expiration date. If a property address has not been
IV. Policies and Procedures 2 of 6 Document #4121
08/03/2022

--- Page 3 ---
Loan Registration and Locking a Loan - Correspondent
provided within the required timeframe the lock will be subject to worse case pricing. Normal extension
guidelines apply when the loan has a property address.
EXTENSIONS
Loans that do not close within the commitment period may be extended for a further period with either a fee
based or a market based extension, whichever is the better option if completed on or before the lock expiration
date. After expiration, only a market based extension is available. Loans that have been expired for >30 days
will be eligible to relock at market.
Lock Extensions are available online at tpo.flagstar.com or by calling the Lock Desk at (866) 945-9872. Refer
to Lock Extension Policy - Correspondent, Doc. #4122 or Mandatory Lock Extension Policy - Correspondent,
Doc. #4123 for applicable guidelines.
CHANGING LOAN PRODUCT OR RATE ON A LOAN LOCKED BEST EFFORTS DELIVERY
When the loan product is changed to a new product from a previously locked-in product, the terms of the new
product may be the worse of:
  The rate and fee of the new product as it was priced on the day the original product was initially locked-
in.
  The current rate and fee of the new product on the day the Lock Desk is contacted to price the product
change.
  Loans that have been submitted to underwriting cannot be locked under the new product until it has
been approved by underwriting.
  Change in product may be subject to worse case pricing, refer to Product Change Guidelines, Doc.
#4124
When a borrower wishes to change the interest rate on a locked loan, the new rate will be priced as follows:
  A request to change interest rate on a locked loan will be priced from the original lock date. Changes to
an interest rate on a locked loan must be completed by contacting the Lock Desk.
  Rate change increases for conventional products, greater than .50, and all rate increases for
Government products will be reviewed by Underwriting for approval.
NEW RATE LOCK FOR PROPERTY ADDRESS CHANGES
The lock is not transferrable for a property address change on an existing commitment. When a new property
address is established a new loan will need to be registered by our Lock Desk at (866) 945-9872. You will be
provided a new loan number in a floating status. Any new rate lock will be based on the current market at the
time of re-commitment. The Lock Desk will monitor property address changes through reporting of duplicate
loans for the same borrower.
LOAN DELIVERY
Flagstar's on-time delivery policy requires the following:
  The complete closed/salable package received by lock expiration.
For complete delivery and post-closing extension guidelines, refer to Correspondent Lock Extension Policy,
Doc. #4122 (p. 3).
IV. Policies and Procedures 3 of 6 Document #4121
08/03/2022

--- Page 4 ---
Loan Registration and Locking a Loan - Correspondent
PAIR-OFFS
If a loan is locked under mandatory commitment, and loan is not closed, disbursed and delivered to Flagstar
according to the lock-in terms, the loan will automatically be subject to pair-off. If Seller does not deliver a
Mortgage Loan locked-in with Flagstar under a best efforts commitment that actually closes, Flagstar may
require Seller to pay a pair-off fee. Pair-off fees will be assessed the day after expiration, and the fees will be
billed to the Correspondent immediately.
Pair-off fees are determined by comparing the current lock-in commitment price with the commitment price that
would apply if the loan was locked on the pair-off date. Both commitment prices should include any applicable
pricing adjustments for that particular loan.
  If the lock-in commitment price on the pair-off date is worse than the locked commitment price (rates
have increased), the pair-off fee will be the difference between a mandatory delivery lock and a best
efforts delivery lock for that particular loan multiplied by the mortgage principal balance.
  If the lock-in commitment price on the pair-off date is better than the locked commitment price (rates
have decreased), the pair-off is calculated as the difference between a mandatory delivery lock and a
best efforts delivery lock for that particular loan plus the price improvement in the market multiplied by
the mortgage balance.
As a result of the pair-off, the existing lock commitment is rendered null and void. If the same loan is re-
submitted for purchase, it will be treated as a new lock and will be priced according to current market
conditions.
SUBSTITUTIONS
If Correspondent cannot deliver a loan that is subject to a mandatory commitment, Correspondent may
substitute an approved loan of the same type, provided that the interest rate of the substituted loan is the same
as the loan being substituted for. A tolerance of 10% of the loan amount will be allowed on deliveries.
For example; if a loan is committed under a mandatory commitment for $150,000 and the loan must be
substituted, Correspondent may deliver another loan within a range of $135,000 - $165,000 to make good
delivery. If Correspondent is unable to make substitution within this range, Flagstar Bank will accept delivery of
the loan but will adjust the pricing accordingly.
For example; if the substituted loan is $200,000, the loan amount will be adjusted and will fund at the original
buy price, however, an over delivery fee will be assessed with the following calculation:
For example;
If the substituted loan is $200,000
$200,000 - $165,000 = $35,000
$35,000 x normal pair off fee calculation (See the Pair-Offs section for additional information)
The over delivery fee will be netted out at funding. Under delivery will result in a pair-off calculation on the
amount not delivered after tolerance.
DENIED LOANS
If a loan that is subject to a best-effort commitment is denied, the existing commitment may be subject to worse

RESCINDED LOANS
If a loan is rescinded the existing commitment becomes subject to worse case pricing if resubmitted. The terms
of this commitment will be the original locked-in rate and fee, or the current market rate and fee, whichever is
worse.
PULLING LOCKED-IN LOANS
We do not want any correspondent to lock-in a loan with Flagstar Bank if the loan is still currently locked-in with
another institution. Similarly, we do not want any correspondent to pull any loans locked-in with Flagstar Bank
so that they can deliver them elsewhere. If we feel that a correspondent is abusing this delivery policy, this
matter will be referred to senior management and/or to legal counsel.
Flagstar Bank reserves the right to impose a substantial monetary penalty if a locked-in loan is pulled and
delivered elsewhere. Any correspondent who closes a loan and sells it to another institution when it has been
previously locked in at Flagstar Bank may be subject to a permanent termination of any business relationship.
Please be aware that Flagstar Bank will be monitoring fall-out ratios and locked loans that do not close within a
timely manner for possible abuses.
CANCELLING A REGISTERED LOAN
In the event that a loan registered with Flagstar must be cancelled using the Cancel Loan link on the Loan
Information page on tpo.flagstar.com, submit the Loan Cancellation/Withdrawal Form, Doc. #3104 via fax to
(248) 312-6929 or email to LockDesk@flagstar.com.
FALLOUT
Lock fallout ratios contribute largely in the star rating calculation which directly impacts your pricing and
company status with Flagstar. Your Star Rating is accessible through your Customer Profile Report on our
website. Refer to Star Rating Formulas in the Reports menu for details concerning the calculation of your star

will need to be completed by the Lock Desk.

RELOCKING A LOAN
A relock is required when a lock commitment has expired or the maximum number or extensions has been
reached. The relock will be calculated at the lesser of the expired lock price or current market price -.125. A
relock may be committed up to the lesser of the initial lock period or 30 days.
If a lock has been expired for 30 days or more it is eligible for a new market lock without additional adjustment
to pricing.
RELOCKING A LOAN (ADVANTAGE PLUS)
A relock is required when a lock commitment has expired or the maximum number or extensions has been
reached. The relock will be calculated at the lesser of the expired lock price or current market price. There is
an additional -.300 applied to a relock. A relock may be committed for a lock period of 30 days.
If a lock has been expired for 45 days or more it is eligible for a new market lock without additional adjustment
to pricing. A relock is also considered mandatory delivery that is subject to a .250 fee if not closed and
delivered.
CURE PERIOD & FUNDING EXTENSION FEE
Flagstar's on time delivery policy requires:
  The complete closed/salable package received by lock expiration.
  Loans that do not meet on-time delivery will be subject to worse case pricing.
Loans delivered on-time by lock expiration date but are incomplete will be given a cure period of 5 business
days (not including weekends and Flagstar observed holidays) following the post-closing problem date or
lock expiration date whichever is greater to resolve outstanding errors and omissions. Loans that do not
have all errors and omissions resolved within this time frame but were delivered on-time will be subject to
an extension fee calculated at 2 bps per diem from the later of lock expiration or post-closing problem date
plus 5 business days. This extension fee will be applied to your loan as a Funding Extension fee. This is a
separate fee and is not netted from the lock price. This fee will apply regardless of an improving or
declining market position.
To ensure purchase of your loans at the existing price, make sure that you are working to deliver complete
and accurate packages on time. Any loan with unresolved errors and omissions after 30 calendar days will
be returned to the correspondent and a marketing fee assessed.
To effectively assist you in making corrections in a timely fashion, please refer to your company s CAD
E&O Report on our website.

EARLY PAYMENT DEFAULT (EPD)
Flagstar shall consider an Early Payment Default when any of the Borrower s first four (4) monthly payments
due to Flagstar becomes 90 days or more delinquent. In the event that any loan sold to Flagstar is classified as
an Early Payment Default, the Seller shall pay Flagstar the following EPD penalty fee:
  0.5% of the loan amount if underwritten by Flagstar
  2.0% of the loan amount if underwritten by Delegated Correspondent.
COLLECTION OF EARLY PAYMENT DEFAULT FEES
A statement will be sent to all Sellers who have loans with early payment defaults on a monthly basis. Payment
for all early payment default fees should be remitted within 30 days of the initial billing. Failure to do so may
result in the deduction of future premiums until the amount due is satisfied.

transaction. Also, all housing expenses, including first and subordinate mortgage loan amounts, property
taxes, homeowner s insurance, flood insurance, association fees, etc., must be included in the debt ratio
calculation.

closing. If they anticipate needing funds prior to that time, they should be encouraged to take those funds as a

Right of Rescission
Under provisions of Section 1026.23 of Regulation Z, which implements the federal Truth in Lending Law, each
borrower, has been given the right to cancel without cost any credit transaction in which a security interest will
be retained or acquired in a borrower s primary dwelling. This right, known as the Right of Rescission, extends
the loan transaction for three (3) business days after a  triggering event  (defined below in the Rescission
Period section).
These guidelines delineate the criteria under which Lenders are required to acknowledge this right and
procedural requirement of Flagstar.
It is important that you read and follow the instructions provided below if you receive a written notice indicating
the borrower is exercising their right to rescind.
TRANSACTIONS EXEMPT FROM THE RIGHT OF RESCISSION
  Residential mortgage transactions, which are transactions for the purchase of the consumer s
principal residence;
  Refinance transactions not involving the principal residence of the consumer;
REGULATORY REQUIREMENTS
Each borrower, including any non-obligated borrower(s), whose ownership interest is or will be subject to the
security interest has the right to rescind the transaction. This applies to closed-end and open-end first and
second lien transactions. Each borrower with the right to rescind, must be provided with two (2) copies each of
the Notice of Right to Rescind (Notice of Right to Cancel) and one copy of the Closing Disclosure (CD).
The Notice of Right to Rescind (or Notice of Right to Cancel) must disclose the following:
  That the transaction involves the Lender obtaining a security interest in the consumer residence
  That the borrower has the right to rescind, joint owners have the right to rescind, and a rescission by
one is effective for all
  Instructions for exercising the right to rescind, with the address of the creditor s place of business;
  The consequences of rescission
  The expiration date of the rescission period
The Closing Disclosure will be considered accurate for purposes of Right of Rescission 1026.23(g) if the
finance charge meets the following:
  Is understated by no more than   of 1 percent of the face of the amount of the note or $100.00,
whichever is greater
  Is greater than the amount required to be disclosed.
FLAGSTAR REQUIREMENT
Flagstar requires that each borrower that is provided a Notice of Right to Cancel acknowledge the receipt of
that document by signing and dating it on the acknowledgment lines provided, and in some cases, the security
document (Mortgage/Deed of Trust).
RESCISSION PERIOD
The rescission period officially begins after the last of three triggering events occur, defined as the last
occurrence of any of the following events (under most normal transactions, all of the following events will occur
at the time the loan documents are signed by the borrower(s) and notarized):
IV. Policies and Procedures 1 of 4 Document #4622
Return to Top 07/15/2022

--- Page 2 ---
Right of Rescission
  Consummation of the transaction (signing of the Note);
  Date the Closing Disclosure is received by the consumer;
  Date the Notice of Right to Cancel (Notice of Right to Cancel) is received by the borrower(s).
Section 1026.23(a)(3) of Regulation Z states the rescission period officially expires at midnight of the third (3rd)
business day after the last occurrence of any of the above events. Funds will not be and are not allowed to be
disbursed until after midnight of the third (3rd) business day.
Notice: If the Lender fails to provide a proper Notice of Right to Cancel or an accurate Closing Disclosure (CD),
the rescission period of time can be extended for up to three (3) years.
See procedures below that must be followed when a Notice of Right to Cancel has been received or when any
other type of notification that a loan has been rescinded has been received.
BUSINESS DAYS
For purposes of rescission, Flagstar Bank, N.A. considers Monday through Saturday to be business days.
Sundays and legal holidays are not considered business days, and thus are not included in the rescission
period.
LEGAL HOLIDAYS
  Christmas Day   New Year s Day
  Columbus Day   President s Day
  Fourth of July   Thanksgiving Day
  Labor Day   Veteran s Day
  Martin Luther King Jr. Day
  Juneteenth
  Memorial Day
BORROWER WAIVER OF RIGHT TO RESCIND
Under certain, very limited circumstances, which are outlined in Regulation Z 1026.23(e), a borrower may
modify or waive his or her right to rescind.
In the event that a consumer inquiries about waiving his or her right to rescind, or inquiries about receiving the
loan proceeds without waiting for the three-day rescission period, a bona fide personal financial emergency
must be proven.
The existence of the borrower s waiver of their right to rescind their loan will not insulate Flagstar Bank, N.A.
from liability for failing to provide the right of rescission. The decision to accept the borrower s request for such
a waiver will be made on a case-by-case basis, considering, among other factors, the personal financial
emergency that must be met before the expiration of the rescission period.
The decision to accept a waiver or modification can only be made through the collaboration of Flagstar s Legal
department, executive and senior management of the business unit.
The borrower must submit a dated written statement that specifically waives or modifies the right and also
includes a description of the emergency. Each borrower entitled to rescind must sign the waiver. The waiver
must be handwritten. Printed forms are prohibited.
IV. Policies and Procedures 2 of 4 Document #4622
Return to Top 07/15/2022

--- Page 3 ---
Right of Rescission
Requests for Waiver of Rescission should be submitted to the Rescission department via email to
FundingAdjustment@Flagstar.com. The Legal department will be notified by the Rescission area, and the
waiver will be supplied to them for their review. The final decision will be relayed to the Mortgage Broker.
IMPORTANT CLOSING INSRUCTIONS
All closing packages, which require a Right to Rescind Notice, must include two (2) copies for each borrower.
This includes borrowers, co-borrowers, and non-obligators.
CHANGES TO THE TRANSACTION
The issuance of any revised documents must be reviewed by the Funding department prior to disbursement of
the funds. If changes are detected during the review of the file in Post-Closing, that area will pursue the signing
of a revised Notice of Right to Cancel from the borrower.
BORROWER REQUIREMENTS TO EXERCISE THE RIGHT TO RESCIND
  The borrower must exercise the right of rescission in writing. The written request must be signed and
dated, but it does not necessarily need to be on the Notice of Right to Cancel form provided.
  If received by mail or email, the notice must be sent no later than midnight of the date on the Note of
Right to Rescind.
  If sent or delivered in another way, the written request to rescind must be delivered to the address
shown on the notice provided no later than midnight of the date on the notice.
EFFECTS OF RESCISSION
The regulation considers a rescinded loan a voided loan. The rescinded status provides for a permanent
cancellation of that loan number and corresponding loan information. This status can never be removed. All
borrowers that wish to re-close their loans must re-apply for a new loan. The rescinded number is no longer an
active number and future activity cannot occur.
NOTIFICATION TO FLAGSTAR BANK OF CONSUMER INTENTION TO RESCIND
Under Section 1026.23(d) of Regulation Z, when a borrower rescinds a transaction, the security interest giving
rise to the right of the rescission becomes void and the consumer shall not be liable for any amount, including
any finance charges or fees paid to a third-party vendor outside of closing.  Any amount  includes the finance
charges already accrued, as well as other charges, such as originator fees, application and commitment fees,
or fees for a title search or appraisal, whether to be paid to the creditor, paid directly to the third party, or
passed on from the creditor to the third party. It is irrelevant that these amounts may not represent profit to the
creditor.
Within 20 calendar days, after receipt of the notice of cancellation/rescission, the creditor has certain
responsibilities to the borrower. The 20-calendar day timeline must be met. The creditor s responsibilities are
as follows:
  The creditor must return any money or property to the borrower that was given to anyone in connection
with the transaction.
  The creditor must take the necessary action to reflect the termination of the security interest.
It is imperative that immediate actions are taken by the originator, settlement agent, and any employee of
Flagstar Bank, N.A. who receives written notice from a borrower that has exercised their right to rescind at any
time.
IV. Policies and Procedures 3 of 4 Document #4622
Return to Top 07/15/2022

--- Page 4 ---
Right of Rescission
When a rescission occurs and a notice is received on any and all residential mortgage loans, it must be
reported to the rescission department in funding immediately upon receipt, regardless of the date it was signed
by the borrower.
The funding department is responsible for processing all residential mortgage loan rescissions. The rescission
department will review the document and make the determination if it should be escalated to Legal and
Compliance for review.
When a borrower exercises their right to rescind on a loan, the following must be followed:
The borrower(s) should immediately forward the executed Notice of Right to Cancel (Notice of Right to Cancel)

department.

during the day. The actual rates, prices and fees applicable to a given commitment will be those in effect at the
time the commitment is obtained.
Flagstar publishes daily price indications at 10 a.m. Eastern Time, should market conditions warrant a change
new price indication sheets will be published and posted at tpo.flagstar.com. It is our intention to notify
customers by e-mail when rates move; however, rates are subject to change at any time without notice.
The most current Price Indications are always available at tpo.flagstar.com.
Please make sure that you click "refresh" or "reload" to make sure that your browser is displaying the most
current price indication sheets.

allows you to enter loan specific details to obtain a price indication on one product or compare pricing on
multiple products. From Price a Loan, you can also register and lock a loan.

registration information. If you do not see this option, contact your website Administrator (usually an officer
of your company) to have your user profile updated with this feature.

your Account Executive for more details.

Eastern Time. To register and/or lock by fax, you must complete the Loan Registration and Lock Request,
Doc. #3101 in its entirety and fax to (248) 312-LOCK (5625).

Correspondent Legal Guide
THE CORRESPONDENT LEGAL GUIDE AND DEFINITIONS
This Chapter of the Guide includes representations, warranties, requirements and obligations of the Seller
which are in addition to, and not in place of, the Seller s obligations contained in the Loan Purchase Agreement
or any other document between Flagstar and Seller. This Chapter is applicable only to Sellers who have
executed a Loan Purchase Agreement on or after November 15, 2018. Sellers who executed a Loan
Purchase Agreement prior to November 15, 2018 shall still be subject to Section 4001  Legal Guide. 
All guidance and information contained in the Guide, including this Chapter, should in no way be construed as
an offer of legal advice by Flagstar or its affiliates. While the Guide provides helpful tools, policies, procedures
and requirements, the Seller should seek independent legal opinion(s) from qualified sources for all legal
determinations, including with respect to any individual Mortgage Loan.
For purposes of the Loan Purchase Agreement and this Chapter of the Guide, the following capitalized terms
have the meanings specified in this Section:
AGENCY OR AGENCIES
The Federal National Mortgage Association ( Fannie Mae ), Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corporation
( Freddie Mac ), Government National Mortgage Association ( Ginnie Mae ), Federal Housing
Administration ( FHA ), Department of Veterans Affairs ( VA ), Department of Housing and Urban
Development ( HUD ), or any other federal or state agency which purchases, insures or guarantees
Mortgage Loans or securities backed by Mortgage Loans.
APPLICABLE LAW
All federal, state and local laws, rules, regulations and regulatory guidance, as amended from time to time,
applicable to the origination, consummation, sale and servicing of Mortgage Loans including, but not limited
to, the Truth in Lending Act and Regulation Z ( TILA ), the Equal Credit Opportunity Act and Regulation B
( ECOA ), the Real Estate Settlement Procedures Act and Regulation X ( RESPA ), the Fair Credit
Reporting Act ( FCRA ), the Flood Disaster Protection Act, the Fair Housing Act, and the Home Mortgage
Disclosure Act and Regulation C ( HMDA ).
BORROWER
The person or persons who submit an application to Seller, receive a Mortgage Loan, and are obligated to
pay under the terms of the Note.
CLOSING
The time when the Borrower signs a Note evidencing a Mortgage Loan and the Mortgage securing
payment of said Note.
COMMITMENT
The written correspondence issued by Flagstar to Seller which indicates Flagstar s agreement to purchase
a specific Mortgage Loan if all conditions stated in the Commitment, the Loan Purchase Agreement, the
Guide, and Investor Guidelines are met.
DISBURSEMENT DATE
The date that funds for a Closing, evidenced by an executed Note, are disbursed on behalf of the Borrower

JUMBO DESK REVIEW
All Jumbo Desk Review orders (regardless of channel) must be placed in Loantrac. Once the order is placed,
Appraisal Management will assign to the appropriate vendor
REQUIREMENTS
  TPO table funded transactions only - Flagstar will disclose a fee to the borrower for the Jumbo Desk
Review on the initial Loan Estimate (LE).
  A standard condition will be applied on all products requiring a Jumbo Desk Review reminding
originators to order the applicable product through Loantrac.
  Attach the appraisal to the order within Loantrac Appraisals under the actions tab when ordering the
Jumbo Desk Review. If you disagree with the value of the appraisal, we strongly recommend that you
dispute the appraisal prior to ordering a Jumbo Desk Review. All Jumbo Desk Reviews will be
delivered to the ValueLink system and must be reviewed by Appraisal Review.
  Non-conforming loans requiring two appraisals due to loan amount or product requirements do not
need a Jumbo Desk Review product. Appraisal Review will review both appraisals and upon
acceptance of both appraisals, the lower value of the two will be considered.
REVIEW OF JUMBO DESK REVIEW APPRAISAL
The Appraisal Management team will perform a review of the appraisal and Jumbo Desk Review product
when both are provided to Flagstar.
  If the value on the Jumbo Desk Review is within 10% of the appraised value, and no material issues
are noted by Appraisal Management the review is complete and Flagstar will accept both reports.
  If the value derived from the Jumbo Desk Review results in a variance of greater than 10%,
Appraisal Management will attempt to reconcile the two reports. If the reports cannot be reconciled
the following will apply:
A full second appraisal will be required and reviewed by Appraisal Review.

TPO Eligibility Standards
Flagstar has established standards to conduct business with all Sellers based on the type of relationship,
which includes Broker, Non-Delegated Correspondent, Delegated Correspondent, and 3rd/4th Party. Flagstar
also maintains standards for additional programs such as appraisal independence, FHA, VA, USDA,
mandatory bulk, etc.
APPROVAL
GENERAL REQUIREMENTS
The following is a list of requirements for all approved Sellers, including Broker, Non-Delegated
Correspondent, Delegated Correspondent and 3rd/4th Party:
  Loan Purchase Agreement including the Mortgage Broker Addendum
  Legal Formation Documents/Certificate of Good Standing
  State Licensing/Registration
  Minimum Mortgage Experience
  Investor Scorecards (if available)
  List of Affiliated Business Arrangements (ABAs)
  Most recent Fiscal Year End Company Financial Statements
  Resumes for all principal officers
  Credit Authorization for all principal offers
  History of Legal and Repurchase Claims
  Quality Control Plan and/or Certification
  TPO Compliance Certification
  Fair Lending Course
  Additional items as determined by Flagstar
NON-DELEGATED CORRESPONDENT
In addition to the items above, the following is a list of requirements for Correspondent approval:
  Evidence of a Warehouse Line (for non-financial institutions)
  Minimum tangible net worth of $100,000
  Fidelity Bond, minimum coverage of $300,000 maximum deductible of $15,000
  E&O Insurance minimum coverage of $300,000 maximum deductible of $15,000
  MERS Lite Approval
  Toll Free/Collect Call Number
DELEGATED CORRESPONDENT
In addition to the items above, the following is a list of requirements for Delegated Correspondent approval:
  Minimum tangible net worth of $1,000,000, evidenced by two most recent years audited Financial
Statements
  Quality Control Plan
  Quality Control Results for the most recent previous two quarters with management s corrective
action plan
  List of Underwriters seeking Delegated authority if tangible net worth is less than $2,500,000
  Company Policies and Procedures (where applicable)

transaction. This time frame is measured from the date the property was no longer listed or offered
for sale to the application date of the current transaction.
DELAYED FINANCING
Borrowers who purchased the subject property within the past six months (measured from the date on
which the property was purchased to the disbursement date of the new mortgage loan) are eligible for a
cash-out refinance if all of the following requirements are met:
  The original purchase transaction was an arms-length transaction.
  The borrower(s) may have initially purchased the property as one of the following:

A natural person; an eligible inter vivos revocable trust, when the borrower is both the individual
o
establishing the trust and the beneficiary of the trust; or
An eligible land trust when the borrower is the beneficiary of the land trust; or an LLC or
o
partnership in which the borrower(s) have an individual or joint ownership of 100%.
The new loan amount can be no more than the actual documented amount of the borrower's initial
investment in purchasing the property plus the financing of closing costs, prepaid fees, and points on the
new mortgage loan (subject to the maximum LTV, CLTV, and HCLTV ratios for the cash-out transaction
based on the current appraised value).
All other cash-out refinance eligibility requirements are met. Cash-out pricing is applicable. Refer to the
Non-Agency guides for all documentation requirements.
CONTINUITY OF OBLIGATION
For a refinance transaction (either rate and term/limited cash-out or cash-out), there must be a continuity of
obligation if there is currently an outstanding lien that will be satisfied through the refinance transaction.
An acceptable Continuity of Obligation exists when any of the following exist:
  There is at least one (1) Borrower obligated on the new loan who was also a Borrower obligated on
the existing loan that is being refinanced;
  The Borrower has been on title and residing in the property for at least six (6) months and has
either paid the mortgage for the last six (6) months or can demonstrate a relationship (parent,
spouse, domestic partner, sibling, etc.) with the current obligor;
  The Borrower has recently inherited or was legally awarded the property (divorce, separation); or
  The existing loan being refinanced and the title have been held in the name of a natural person or a
limited liability company as long as the Borrower was a member of the limited liability company prior
to transfer. The loan must have been transferred out of Limited Liability Company prior to
application. Transfer of ownership from a corporation to individual does not meet Continuity of
Obligation.
NON-ARM S LENGTH TRANSACTION
Non-arm s length transactions involve a personal relationship or business relationship (outside of the
subject transaction) between the Borrower and any interested party to the transaction. These transactions
must be fully disclosed as such and the appraiser must be informed of the non-arm s length transaction
and address whether or not the market value has been affected.
A "family member" is defined as the Borrower's spouse, child, dependent, domestic partner, fianc ,
fianc e, or any other individual related to the borrower by blood, marriage, adoption, or legal guardianship.
Non-arm s length transactions are considered only under the following conditions:
  Relationships are clearly disclosed with initial submission;
  Primary residence only;
  Additional risk factors are not present (i.e., distress sale, selling assets for down
  payment, etc.);
  Loans made to principals or employees of the lender or service provider cannot provide services on
their own transactions (closing agent, title agent, appraiser, etc.); and

the seller must ensure that the Borrower is not one of the owners of the business entity selling the
subject property.
Family transactions occur when a family member deeds the title to their home to another family member.
The following apply to family transactions:
  Relationships are clearly disclosed with initial submission;
  Primary residence only;
  Purchase contract must be provided;
  A Gift of Equity letter is required to explain the relationship and reason for the gift;
  Appraiser must note this is a non-arm s length transaction;
  Foreclosure bailouts are not allowed. Payoff statement and Verification of Mortgage (VOM) on
subject required as verification;
  The HUD-1 must reflect all liens on title are paid and not all loan proceeds going to the family
member; and
  Current appraised value is used for LTV purposes.
SUBORDINATE FINANCING
Subordinate financing must be provided by a financial institution. Employer seconds are not allowed.
Refer to the Non-Agency Underwriting Guidelines for all requirements.
TEXAS REFINANCE LOANS
All refinance loans in Texas will be evaluated against the criteria outlined in our Non-Agency Underwriting
Guidelines, Texas Home Equity/50(a)(6) Right of Rescission section to determine whether or not they must be
originated under the requirements of Section 50(a)(6) of the Texas Constitution. Loans that fall under Section
